summary: A strong Phase 2. The published build serves three genuine bundled recorded sample sets (183 FLACs, 153 MB, all 183 SHA256 digests matching manifest.json, CC-BY-3.0/CC0 from three different publishers, 20-36 roots and 2-4 recorded velocity bands each) and three honestly-declared synthesis types; all six are audibly distinct through the live graph (spectral cosine 0.61-0.88). The effect chain is real streaming DSP in an AudioWorklet: every one of the 25 listed types measurably changes a standardized signal (min pairwise diff 0.0389, all vsDry >= 0.063 except To Rotary, which is a route and was verified through the shared Rotary), reverb decay orders Booth<Room<Spring<Stage<Hall<Cathedral as specified, delay feedback filtering leaves the dry attack bit-identical, bypass is click-free (max jump 5.45e-4) and returns the exact dry signal. Exactly one AudioContext, two layer buses, one shared Rotary, master gain + limiter, one destination, no clipping (peak 0.145 on 12 voices). Chief shortfall: Delay Dry/Wet, delay feedback filter, Amp Drive, Amp Mid Freq, clock sync and Group mode exist only in a supplemental drawer, not on the panel.

evidence: Six types all sound through the published build's live graph and are spectrally distinct. Recording a ScriptProcessor tap on the master gain of build/ (served static, 1440x900, note C4 via real CDP KeyA events) gave RMS Grand 0.005135, Upright 0.017392, Electric 0.020796, Clav 0.003858, Digital 0.010099, Misc 0.007253, with 16-band normalised spectra whose cosine similarity is 0.751 (Grand/Upright), 0.792 (Grand/Electric), 0.613 (Upright/Electric), 0.880 (Clav/Digital), 0.843 (Digital/Misc) — no voice is relabelled.

Grand/Upright/Electric are genuine, independent recorded libraries, not one set re-pitched: build/samples/manifest.json lists 183 entries (Grand 78, Upright 63, Electric 42); every file in build/samples is real FLAC ('fLaC' magic), all 183 SHA256 digests match the manifest, all 183 digests are unique, totalling 153.0 MB. Grand has 26 root notes (MIDI 27-102) and 3 recorded velocity bands, Upright 36 roots (24-108) / 2 bands, Electric 20 roots (33-92) / 4 bands — from three different authors and licences (Alexander Holm CC-BY-3.0, FreePats CC0-1.0, Greg Sullivan CC-BY-3.0).

Per-type model identity reaches the panel: cycling #piano-piano-type six times walked the Program OLED through 'Salamander C5', 'Upright KW', 'Wurlitzer EP200', 'Plucked clav · synthesis', 'FM keys · synthesis', 'Vibraphone · synthesis' and wrapped back to Salamander C5.

Character of the three synthetic types is simplified in ways a player would notice: src/library.ts renderSynthetic is one analytic formula per type (Clav = 12 exponentially-decaying harmonics, Digital = single-operator FM, Misc = three inharmonic partials at 1/2.76/5.4), one model each, no velocity-dependent timbre layers — audibly thinner than the recorded sets and than Nord's Clav/Digital engines.

Every unit and every listed type measurably processes audio. Rendering the published build/audio/dsp.js Unit class at 8 kHz on a standardized 180 Hz + 1730 Hz burst, RMS difference from the same unit bypassed was: mod1 types [0.0824, 0.1225, 0.2387, 0.1949, 0.0865, 0.0609], mod2 [0.1487, 0.1947, 0.1614, 0.1982, 0.1390, 0.1331], ampEq [0.1033, 0.1130, 0.0946, 0.1564, 0.0630, 0.3050, 0.0], reverb [0.2506, 0.1655, 0.2559, 0.1888, 0.2459, 0.2344], delay 0.3019, compressor 0.1318. The single 0.0 is ampEq type 6 'To Rotary', which is a route by design and was verified audible through the shared Rotary separately (routed delta 0.2622 vs unrouted exactly 0.0).

No two types inside a unit render identically: worst-case pairwise RMS difference was mod1 0.0836 (A-Pan vs Tremolo), mod2 0.0524 (Chorus vs Ensemble), ampEq 0.0389 (Twin vs JC), reverb 0.0833 (Room vs Spring).

Namesake behaviour checks out. Reverb tail energy after 1.2 s grows in the specified order — Booth 0.0, Room 5.3e-5, Spring 1.5e-3, Stage 8.9e-3, Hall 1.09e-2, Cathedral 0.1015 — and Spring alone adds a dispersive allpass (build/audio/dsp.js line 62, type===2). Delay feedback filtering processes only the repeats: dry attack difference over the first 800 samples is exactly 0 while the region after 5000 samples differs by 0.0405 (LP), 0.0693 (HP), 0.0617 (BP). Compressor reduces RMS 0.23597 -> 0.05984 from amount 0 to 1.

Confirmed on the live build, not just in the DSP: with Reverb ON, Dry/Wet at max and type cycled to Cathedral, the recorded 8-segment envelope ran 0.00486/0.00759/0.00247/0.00187/0.00141/0.00072/0.00033/0.00020 versus dry 0.01061/0.00150/0/0/0/0/0/0; Delay (0.44 s, feedback 0.85) sustained audible repeats through all 8 segments; Tremolo at 3.07 Hz amplitude-modulated the envelope; the Layer Effects ON button restored the bit-identical dry envelope (0.01059/0.00167/0/0/0/0/0/0).

Bypass is click-free and parameter-accurate: driving mod1 Tremolo at full amount then switching it off gave a maximum inter-sample jump of 5.45e-4 and settled to exactly 0.50000, the dry input value. The full ChainDSP with all units off passes the input through with maximum deviation 0.0.

Two documented approximations a knowledgeable player would notice: Compressor Fast mode changes the rendered signal by only 0.00403 (versus 0.14913 for Amount), and Reverb Bright/Dark by 0.02009; Twin/JC/Small are a shared tanh drive plus a fixed lowpass colour (build/audio/dsp.js line 52, colors [0,3200,6500,1400]) rather than distinct speaker models, which IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json declares.
Exactly one AudioContext in the running build. Wrapping window.AudioContext before the bundle loaded and then clicking 'Enable audio' produced __ctxs.length === 1, state 'running', sampleRate 48000.

Recorded AudioNode.connect edges match the specified order end to end: GainNode(bus) -> AudioWorkletNode(layer chain) for each of two layers, then AudioWorkletNode -> AudioWorkletNode at inputs 0 and 1 (one shared Rotary), Rotary outputs 0 and 1 -> per-layer GainNode levels -> master GainNode -> DynamicsCompressorNode -> AudioDestinationNode. One destination, one limiter, layer level after Rotary — exactly the requiredOrder in specs/nord-stage-4.effects.json. ORDER in build/audio/dsp.js is ['mod1','mod2','delay','ampEq','compressor','reverb'].

Nothing bypasses the master path: setting #performance-master-level to 0 produced a recorded RMS of exactly 0.000000 (all eight envelope segments 0) with a note sounding, and restoring it returned RMS 0.005135.

Sane gain staging with no clipping under load: across all 27 live captures, 0 samples reached |x| >= 0.999; peak was 0.0435 for one Grand note, 0.0869 for two layers, 0.1451 for twelve simultaneous keys. Limiter is a DynamicsCompressor at threshold -3 dB, knee 3, ratio 20, attack 3 ms, release 100 ms (src/layer-audio.ts:26).

Cleanup is real: dispose() kills voices, posts dispose to both chain worklets and the Rotary, closes their ports and disconnects buses, levels, master and limiter (src/layer-audio.ts:81); the artifact's own browser test asserts nodes/buses/chains/master/rotary are all empty afterwards or throws 'Leaked graph'. Zero console errors were logged in any of my six probe sessions against build/.

Both layers reach the audio graph independently. One layer gave recorded RMS 0.005135; clicking #piano-layer-b-on gave 0.010439 (≈2x, two owned voices); setting Layer B's level fader to 0 returned 0.005055, i.e. back to Layer A alone.

Enable, focus and octave all take effect: clicking #piano-layer-b-on moved the Program OLED from 'PIANO A Salamander C5' to 'PIANO B Salamander C5'; src/audio.ts:71-75 starts one voice per enabled layer at pending.note + settings.octave, and src/phase2.test.ts asserts notes [60, 72] with layers ['A','B'] for a +12 shift on B.

Disabling a layer kills only that layer's voices — src/audio.ts:87 kills voices whose layer is disabled while leaving the other layer's held voice intact (phase2.test.ts asserts kills === [2] with voice 1 still held).

FX focus follows layer focus and the panel reflects it: src/panel.ts:11 reads s.layers[s.fxFocus].effects, focusLayer() sets focus, fxFocus and fxSection together (src/instrument.ts:21), and I confirmed the Reverb Amount knob kept the focused layer's value 0.9 with title 'Reverb amount · 0.9' after re-focusing.

One behaviour a player would notice: moving a Layer level fader on the panel also steals layer focus (src/panel.ts:49 calls focusLayer on the target), so trimming Layer B's level silently re-targets piano and FX editing away from A.

KB Touch, Dyn Comp, Unison, Soft Release, String Res and Master Level all measurably change the rendered signal in the published build. Recorded RMS at a fixed synthetic keystroke: Heavy 0.003998 < Medium 0.005220 < Light 0.012663; Dyn Comp 3 raised the soft-stroke level to 0.006538 from 0.005220 at Off (the artifact's own render test asserts this is monotonic across levels 0-3); Unison 3 gave 0.007791 with a changed spectrum (cosine 0.935 against Off) from three detuned sources panned -0.85/0/+0.85 (src/layer-audio.ts:62-64).

Soft Release lengthens the tail: envelope segment 3 read 0.000440 with Soft Release on against 0.000000 off (release 0.48 s vs 0.22 s, src/layer-audio.ts:72), and it is correctly disabled for Clav as the spec requires.

String Res adds sympathetic energy only alongside another held note: holding two keys gave 0.007744 with it on against 0.007174 off, and src/audio.ts:75 passes resonate only when a routed pedal is down or another voice of the same layer is held.
Panel feedback agrees with state for every one of these: control titles read 'KB touch · Medium', 'Dyn comp · 3', 'Timbre · Bright', 'Unison · 3', 'Master level · 0' after driving them.

Timbre is the weakest of the set: switching the Grand from Off to Bright shifted the 2.9-5.1 kHz share of the spectrum only from 1.913% to 2.317% (RMS 0.005220 -> 0.005151). It is a single biquad per voice with fixed frequencies and gains [0,0,5,7,10,-6] dB (src/layer-audio.ts:65), so Dyno 1/Dyno 2 are shelf variants rather than tine preamp emulations — a simplification the notes acknowledge.
Excluded detail is correctly absent rather than faked: there is no pedal-noise or half-pedal control anywhere in the 140-control panel, matching the piano spec's excluded list.

Computer-keyboard input is repeat-safe and polyphonic under stress: five synthetic autoRepeat keydowns on KeyA left exactly 1 key in the pressed state, and holding 17 mapped keys at once lit 17 keys and rendered RMS 0.017460 with peak 0.1451 and zero clipped samples.

Failures degrade visibly. Blocking exactly one of the 183 bundled recordings (*/samples/grand/A1v14.flac via CDP Network.setBlockedURLs) drove the status line to 'Sample failure · playable synthesis fallback · Grand', the Program OLED to 'SAMPLE FAILED · FALLBACK', added the .sample-failure class to the type LEDs, and relabelled the action button 'Retry samples' — while staying playable at RMS 0.007935. The primary library was never reported ready.
Recovery works: unblocking the URL and clicking 'Retry samples' returned the status line to 'Ready · bundled recorded piano library'.

All-notes-off on loss of focus is real: dispatching window blur while 17 keys were held left 0 keys pressed (src/inputs.ts:12 clears held and calls engine.allOff; src/App.tsx:44 adds the same on visibilitychange and disposes engine and MIDI on unmount).

MIDI reports its own state rather than pretending: the utility button read 'MIDI: not connected' and became 'MIDI: denied' after a denied requestMIDIAccess in the headless probe; src/inputs.ts:18-36 distinguishes unavailable, denied, no devices, connected and disconnected, and calls engine.allOff() when a port is lost.

Zero console errors or page errors were recorded across six separate probe sessions against build/ (CDP Log.entryAdded level=error and Runtime.exceptionThrown both empty), and 0 network requests failed on a clean load.

All six required types are present and selectable from the hardware panel: #piano-piano-type cycles Grand -> Upright -> Electric -> Clav -> Digital -> Misc -> Grand, and the six type LEDs render in the Piano section (.type-labels). A redundant select (#setting-piano-type) reaches the same state.

All six actually load and produce audio in the published build — measured RMS 0.005135 / 0.017392 / 0.020796 / 0.003858 / 0.010099 / 0.007253 respectively, with distinct spectra (see instrumentBreadth).

The three required recorded sets load offline from the published build: build/samples holds grand/, upright/ and electric/ plus each publisher's LICENSE and README, 183 FLAC files verified byte-for-byte against manifest.json SHA256 digests, served from the same origin with no network calls (0 failed requests, status 'Ready · bundled recorded piano library').

The optional multi-model features are honestly skipped rather than faked: the Model dial reports 'One bundled model per type' as its value text, and IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json unsupported[2] declares model list, size classes and INFO view as absent.

All six units plus the shared Rotary exist with every listed type reachable: the panel effects section carries 29 controls (effects-mod-1-{rate,amount,type,on}, effects-mod-2-{...}, effects-eq-{bass,mid,treble}, effects-amp-model, effects-amp-eq-on, effects-delay-{time,feedback,tap,on}, effects-compressor-{amount,dry-wet,mode,on}, effects-reverb-{amount,tone,type,on}) and the Rotary lives in the Performance section (performance-rotary-{drive,on,slow-fast,stop-mode,source}). Type cycling covers mod1 6, mod2 6, ampEq 7 including 'To Rotary', reverb 6 (src/instrument.ts:5).

Routing controls are on the panel and functional: effects-organ-focus / effects-piano-focus / effects-synth-focus set FX section, effects-effects-on is the all-effects bypass (verified to restore the bit-identical dry envelope on the live build), and Shift + a unit's On toggles global mode for Delay/Compressor/Reverb (src/panel.ts:65).

Routing into the Rotary works from the panel: cycling #effects-amp-model to 'To Rotary', enabling that unit and turning on #performance-rotary-on and #performance-rotary-slow-fast raised the recorded RMS to 0.005743 with a modulated envelope running out to segment 6, versus dry dying at segment 2.

Shortfall against 'reachable from the panel': six required parameters exist only in the supplemental 'Piano & effects settings' drawer beneath the instrument, not as panel controls — Delay Dry/Wet (#setting-delay-dry-wet), Delay feedback filter Off/LP/HP/BP (#setting-delay-feedback-filter), Amp Drive (#setting-amp-drive), Amp Mid/Filter Frequency (#setting-eq-mid-filter-frequency), Master Clock sync for Mod 1/Mod 2/Delay (#setting-mod1-clock-sync etc.) and Group mode (#setting-piano-group). The panel's Delay group has only Time and Feedback knobs where the hardware also has Dry/Wet, and there is no Group control on the panel at all.

The drawer parameters do reach audio, so this is placement rather than absence: enabling Delay from the drawer at Dry/Wet 1, 0.4 s and feedback 0.85 produced repeats across all eight envelope segments (0/0.0113/0.0099/0.0075/0.0058/0.0052/0.0042/0.0032) against a dry envelope that reached 0 by segment 2.

With Organ or Synth FX focus selected the panel effect knobs still present live-looking titles and values but silently snap back (setting Reverb Amount to 20 under Organ focus left it at 0.9); it refuses rather than fakes, but nothing on the panel says the target is unavailable.

Decorative claims verified by measurement, not by reading: of the 140 panel controls in the running build, 90 carry '(decorative)' in their accessible name and '— presentation only' in their title, and 50 are live. #organ-drawbar-16 reads 'Drawbar 16 — presentation only' and the Synth OLED reads 'SYNTH OFFLINE / Phase 2 / Decorative controls', matching unsupported[0]. All 140 are operable and hit-testable (0 unreachable under a 5x5 elementFromPoint grid at 1440x900; 0 missing aria-labels).

Declared-unsupported items really are absent: no soft or sostenuto pedal control exists anywhere (unsupported[1], and no approximation is claimed); performance-rotary-stop-mode and performance-rotary-source are excluded from functional() in src/panel.ts:9 as declared; src/inputs.ts:38-44 handles only note on/off, CC64 and CC120/123, so the declared absence of pitch bend, aftertouch and program change is accurate; program-master-clock is decorative while the effects clock is a separately disclosed drawer control.

Source honesty is exact. IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json and build/samples/ATTRIBUTION.md name the three recorded libraries with author, publisher URL, licence and 'no modifications', and separately label Clav/Digital/Misc, the simulated resonance and the failure fallback as original generated PCM — and the files back that up (183 verified FLACs; renderSynthetic in src/library.ts is analytic). No generated source is described as a recording.

The declared gap about sample density is truthful and checkable: Electric roots are indeed sparser at the top (20 roots spanning MIDI 33-92, so E1 and E7 are transposed from outside the recorded range), Grand roots are minor-third spaced with 3 recorded velocity bands, Upright has 2 bands — exactly as declaredGaps[2] states.

Undeclared shortfall: nothing in unsupported or declaredGaps states that Delay Dry/Wet, the delay feedback filter, Amp Drive, Amp Mid Freq, clock sync and Group mode are absent from the hardware panel and reachable only from the drawer. declaredGaps[1] mentions that 'supplemental settings sit below the instrument' but does not identify these required effect parameters as panel-absent, so a reader of the declaration would not learn of the gap.

issues.title: Six required effect parameters are reachable only from the supplemental drawer, not the panel
issues.detail: The panel's Layer Effects section holds 29 controls and its Delay group has only Time, Feedback, Tap and On. Delay Dry/Wet, the Delay feedback filter (Off/LP/HP/BP), Amp Drive, Amp Mid/Filter Frequency, Master Clock sync for Mod 1/Mod 2/Delay, and Group mode exist only as #setting-delay-dry-wet, #setting-delay-feedback-filter, #setting-amp-drive, #setting-eq-mid-filter-frequency, #setting-mod1-clock-sync/#setting-mod2-clock-sync/#setting-delay-clock-sync and #setting-piano-group inside the collapsed 'Piano & effects settings' drawer below the instrument. All of them do reach audio (drawer-driven Delay at Dry/Wet 1, 0.4 s, feedback 0.85 produced repeats across all eight recorded envelope segments), so this is control placement rather than missing behaviour — but specs/nord-stage-4.effects.json lists them as required unit parameters and the real panel carries a Dry/Wet knob and a Group path.

issues.title: Panel-absent effect parameters are not named in the declared gaps
issues.detail: IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json declaredGaps[1] notes only that 'supplemental settings sit below the instrument, closed by default'. It does not say which required effect parameters (Delay Dry/Wet, feedback filter, Amp Drive, Amp Mid Freq, clock sync, Group) are unavailable on the panel itself, so the declaration does not disclose the gap a panel-driven evaluation finds.

issues.title: Compressor Fast mode and Reverb Bright/Dark are near-inaudible
issues.detail: Rendering build/audio/dsp.js at 8 kHz on a standardized burst, switching the compressor between Normal and Fast at amount 1 changed the signal by an RMS difference of only 0.00403, and sweeping Reverb Bright/Dark from 0 to 1 by 0.02009 — against 0.14913 for compressor Amount and 0.31326 for reverb Dry/Wet. The manual describes Fast mode as recovering quicker and pumping at high amounts, which this attack/release change (2/45 ms vs 12/250 ms) barely delivers on the rendered signal.

issues.title: Timbre's effect on the acoustic pianos is very subtle
issues.detail: Switching the Grand from Timbre Off to Bright moved the 2.9-5.1 kHz share of the recorded live-graph spectrum only from 1.913% to 2.317% (RMS 0.005220 -> 0.005151). It is one biquad per voice with fixed frequency and gains [0,0,5,7,10,-6] dB (src/layer-audio.ts:65); Dyno 1 and Dyno 2 are further shelf variants rather than tine preamp emulations. The control is measurable and honestly documented, but shallower than the manual's Soft/Mid/Bright/Dyno description.

issues.title: Moving a Layer level fader steals layer and FX focus
issues.detail: src/panel.ts:49 calls focusLayer(state, target) whenever piano-layer-a-level or piano-layer-b-level changes, so trimming Layer B's level silently re-targets piano editing and the effect chain from A to B. I confirmed the side effect while probing: adjusting Layer B's fader moved subsequent effect edits onto Layer B's chain. Related: the drawer summary continued to read 'FX Piano A' after #effects-organ-focus set the FX section to Organ.

issues.title: Panel effect knobs are silently inert under Organ/Synth FX focus
issues.detail: With #effects-organ-focus selected, src/panel.ts:63 gates effect edits on fxSection === 'Piano', so setting #effects-reverb-amount to 20 left it at its previous 0.9 with the title still reading 'Reverb amount · 0.9'. The control refuses rather than faking success, and IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json notes[3] calls this 'a visibly unavailable audio target', but nothing on the panel itself marks the knobs as unavailable in that state.
